title: SSRF in OpenClaw Image tool remote fetch
summary: The Image tool fetched attacker-supplied HTTP(S) URLs without SSRF protection, enabling requests to localhost, private, link-local and cloud-metadata targets. The upstream advisory notes GET-only behavior, media-type validation and metadata-service header requirements, which limit some direct confidentiality scenarios.
ai_role: Endor Labs’ case-specific report describes its AI SAST engine’s trace for this finding and the researcher’s subsequent validation with a proof of concept. This supports AI-assisted discovery with human validation; the specific model is not named. The six-case article was updated after initial publication, so the exact first public date of its current attribution text is not established.
classification_note: The upstream security advisory documents the public disclosure and fix. The sources do not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: OpenClaw 2026.2.2 and later are listed as patched; remote media fetching now uses the SSRF guard with internal/private host checks, redirect hardening and DNS pinning.

impacts.conditions: The Image tool must fetch an attacker-controlled URL; requests are GET-only and fetched content must pass image/media validation. Metadata services requiring special headers/tokens may not be reachable for direct credential theft.
impacts.exploitation: The sources report validation or describe attack conditions but do not report observed exploitation.
